issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture fields using snake_case names (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods use camelCase field names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This name mismatch causes undefined field references and compilation errors, preventing students from running or using the provided solution and creating confusion about the correct attribute names from the UML/problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent across the class. Rename the declared fields in the solution to use the camelCase names shown in the UML and used by the constructor/methods (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or update the constructor and all methods to reference the snake_case field names. Prefer matching the UML/camelCase naming to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify attribute names in camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution repository declares the corresponding private fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while its constructor and methods use the camelCase names. This naming mismatch within the solution (and between solution and problem) creates a direct mapping/confusion for students and will cause incorrect bindings or compile errors since used identifiers do not match the declared fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the private field names in the solution to match the UML/problem camelCase identifiers and the constructor/method usage. For example: private String lectureName; private int numberOfInscribedStudents; private int numberOfGuestStudents; private int numberOfLecturers; private int numberOfTutors; and ensure all references use these names (e.g., this.lectureName = lectureName;).
